audit_summary.overall_outcome: Seven compliance agents were reviewed for case TEST-2024-001 (LN-2024-001). No agent returned a clean Pass. HVCRE returned Not Applicable (Non-HVCRE classification, high confidence, no deficiencies beyond minor file notation gaps). FZD returned Compliant with Moderate confidence, subject to documentation gaps. HMDA, ECOA, HPML, YBS, and VMI all returned Potential Issue or Non-Compliant. Three cross-regime deficiency clusters were identified: (1) a rate spread and APR data contradiction affecting HMDA, ECOA, and HPML across all three regimes simultaneously; (2) a systemic demographic data and VMI documentation deficiency affecting HMDA and VMI and cross-cutting ECOA fair lending obligations; and (3) a systemic missing-evidence pattern affecting YBS, ECOA, HMDA, and HPML, centered on absent income, applicant identity, and co-borrower documentation. Additional isolated findings exist in HPML (appraisal delivery obligations, TRID Loan Estimate absence, flip-rule analysis gap) and FZD (flood determination metadata completeness, life-of-loan monitoring gap). The loan file in its current state is not examination-ready under FCA standards for any of the five regimes returning Potential Issue or Non-Compliant determinations.

cross_regime_findings.root_cause: Rate Spread and APR/APOR Data Contradiction
cross_regime_findings.impact_summary: All three agents independently flagged the same irreconcilable discrepancy: the HMDA rate spread field reports 2.37 percentage points, while the structured APR (8.12%) and APOR (7.02%) fields produce a calculated spread of 1.10 percentage points. This single data error has cascading regulatory consequences across three regimes. For HMDA, the rate spread is a required LAR data field; an inaccurate value constitutes a material reporting deficiency subject to resubmission and FCA examination citation. For ECOA and HPML, the spread determines whether the loan is a first-lien Higher-Priced Mortgage Loan under Regulation Z (threshold: 1.50 pp). If the spread is 1.10 pp, HPML obligations do not attach; if 2.37 pp is correct, HPML status is confirmed, triggering mandatory escrow, appraisal independence, appraisal delivery, right-to-receive notice, ability-to-repay documentation, and flip-rule analysis requirements—all of which interact with ECOA fair lending and examination readiness obligations. The APOR source document (specific FFIEC weekly table entry for lock date 2024-04-10) and the APR calculation worksheet are absent from the file for all three agents, preventing resolution. The rate lock agreement is also absent, preventing independent verification of the correct APOR comparison date.

cross_regime_findings.root_cause: Demographic Data Not Extracted or Recorded Despite Confirmed VMI Collection
cross_regime_findings.impact_summary: HMDA, VMI, and ECOA each independently identified that the demographic information block (ethnicity, race, sex) is entirely empty for both the primary applicant (John Smith) and the co-applicant (Mary Smith), despite vmi_presented_to_applicant and applicant_provided_vmi both being flagged true. This creates an internal data inconsistency: process flags indicate collection occurred, but no collected values exist in any record field. This single root cause simultaneously produces: a HMDA LAR reporting deficiency (12 CFR 1003.4(a)(10)(i)-(ii) requires ethnicity, race, and sex for both applicants); a Regulation B / 12 CFR 1002.13 record-keeping deficiency (collected data must be retained); a VMI documentation deficiency (no form identifier, no collection date, no co-applicant record, no refusal documentation, no applicant acknowledgment of voluntary nature); and a fair lending examination gap under ECOA (consistency of treatment analysis requires demographic records). Additionally, disaggregated ethnicity and race sub-categories required by the 2018 HMDA rule are absent. The firewall and segregation controls are asserted by boolean flags only, without corroborating audit logs or access reports, which all three agents flagged as insufficient for examination purposes.

cross_regime_findings.root_cause: Systemic Missing Income, Identity, and Co-Borrower Documentation Across Regimes
cross_regime_findings.impact_summary: Five agents independently identified overlapping gaps in borrower income documentation, applicant identity documentation, and co-borrower (Mary Smith) data. HMDA requires gross annual income relied on in the credit decision for LAR reporting (12 CFR 1003.4(a)(10)(iii)); the income field is absent. HPML requires documented income verification for ability-to-repay under 12 CFR 1026.43 for a first-lien HPML; income verification documents (tax returns, Schedule F, farm financial statements) are not confirmed in the file. YBS requires gross agricultural sales documentation via Schedule F or tax returns to confirm the Small Farmer threshold, and requires government-issued ID or birth certificate for both borrowers to confirm Young Farmer age eligibility. ECOA notes the absence of individual credit reports for each joint applicant, preventing independent creditworthiness verification and fair lending consistency review. VMI notes the complete absence of co-applicant (Mary Smith) data of any kind, including age, farming experience, demographic information, and YBS eligibility, despite the joint application. This pattern reflects a systemic documentation standard deficiency: the file was assembled with primary closing instruments but lacks the underlying borrower-evidence layer required for multi-regime regulatory examination readiness. The shared root cause is the absence of a file assembly standard that requires retention of income verification, identity, and co-borrower documentation as a baseline for all covered transactions.

cross_regime_findings.root_cause: Manual Underwrite Without Quality Control or Secondary Review Documentation
cross_regime_findings.impact_summary: HMDA, ECOA, and HPML each noted that the transaction was manually underwritten with no AUS result, and that no quality control or secondary review sign-off appears in the supporting documents. HMDA requires proper LAR AUS coding (FIG 2024 code 1111 for Not Applicable) supported by documentation confirming no AUS was used. ECOA identifies manual underwrite as an elevated disparate treatment risk vector; FCA fair lending guidance requires documentation of the manual underwrite rationale and consistency of application across the portfolio, particularly for joint applications and YBS-classified borrowers. HPML notes that for a provisionally classified HPML transaction, manual underwrite files must demonstrate ability-to-repay compliance under 12 CFR 1026.43, and the absence of income documentation and QC sign-off compounds this gap. The shared root cause is the absence of a manual underwrite documentation standard requiring secondary review, rationale documentation, and QC sign-off at origination.

cross_regime_findings.root_cause: YBS Designation Not Documented Despite Facial Triple Qualification and FCA Reporting Obligations
cross_regime_findings.impact_summary: Both YBS and ECOA independently identified that the primary borrower (John Smith, age 34, 4 years farming, $185,000 gross farm sales) facially satisfies all three FCA YBS criteria simultaneously—Young, Beginning, and Small—yet no YBS designation form, YBS plan cross-reference, or documentation of whether YBS-specific rates, terms, or services were considered or offered exists in the file. FCA Regulation 4.20 and 12 CFR 614.4165 require Farm Credit ACAs to maintain YBS plans and document YBS status at origination. Failure to designate a qualifying borrower creates FCA Call Report data integrity risk and may indicate underservice of a statutorily protected class of agricultural borrowers. ECOA additionally flags that the age field (age 34) is used for YBS classification as a favorable differentiation, which is permissible, but the distinction between favorable YBS age use and prohibited adverse age consideration under Regulation B must be documented explicitly. The co-borrower Mary Smith has no age or farming experience data, leaving her YBS eligibility entirely unaddressed.

No evidence of delivery or issuance exists. If HPML status is confirmed upon APR/APOR reconciliation, this constitutes a documented regulatory violation. Additionally, no evidence exists that the appraisal was delivered to the applicants at least 3 business days before consummation (required by approximately 2024-04-26 under 12 CFR 1026.35(c)(6)(i)); the appraisal was received by the institution on 2024-03-28 making timely delivery feasible, but no delivery log, borrower receipt, or transmittal evidence is present. The additional appraisal (flip-rule) analysis required under 12 CFR 1026.35(c)(4) for first-lien HPML purchase transactions on existing properties is not documented. The file asserts additional_appraisal_required = false but contains no prior sale history from title or county records and no documented analysis of whether the flip-rule price-increase thresholds were evaluated. Life-of-loan flood monitoring enrollment is not documented, representing an ongoing compliance obligation gap. Additionally, the 240-acre farm may contain agricultural structures beyond the principal dwelling; there is no evidence that all improved structures on the parcel were individually identified and evaluated for SFHA exposure. FZD remains the only agent returning Compliant, but confidence is limited to Moderate by these documentation gaps.

The NMLS identifier provided (987654) has not been confirmed as the individual loan originator's NMLS ID versus an institution-level identifier; 12 CFR 1003.4(a)(34) requires the individual originator's ID. No compliance deficiency exists; these are examination-readiness improvements only.

audit_determination_summary.audit_narrative: Case TEST-2024-001 presents a loan file with sound primary closing documentation and internally consistent origination chronology, but with a systemic failure to retain the secondary evidentiary layer required for multi-regime regulatory examination readiness. Three structural deficiencies drive the majority of cross-regime findings. First, a single rate spread data error in the HMDA fields (2.37 pp reported versus 1.10 pp calculated from the supplied APR and APOR) propagates across HMDA, ECOA, and HPML simultaneously, affecting LAR data accuracy, HPML classification, and the scope of Regulation Z obligations. This is the highest-priority remediation item because its resolution determines the regulatory footprint of the entire file. Second, the demographic data block is empty despite affirmative process flags indicating collection occurred, creating simultaneous deficiencies under HMDA (LAR reporting), VMI (record-keeping and form documentation), and ECOA (fair lending examination support). The absence of co-applicant (Mary Smith) data across all regimes—demographics, age, farming experience, YBS eligibility—reflects a systemic gap in joint-borrower documentation. Third, income verification documents, borrower identity documents, and co-borrower data are absent from the file, producing overlapping findings across HMDA (income field), HPML (ATR), YBS (sales and age documentation), ECOA (credit report and fair lending consistency), and VMI (co-applicant demographics). These three root causes share a common institutional origin: the file was built around execution documents (note, mortgage, closing disclosure, appraisal, commitment letter) without a corresponding retention standard for the underlying borrower-evidence, demographic-data, and regulatory-determination documentation required for examination readiness across the institution's full regulatory compliance footprint. The HPML agent's Non-Compliant determination—the only outright Non-Compliant result—is the most acute finding in the file and is contingent on the rate spread remaining unresolved. If the rate spread is confirmed at 1.10 pp upon reconciliation, the HPML determination would likely resolve to Not Applicable or Pass, substantially reducing the regulatory severity of the file. If the rate spread is confirmed at or above 1.50 pp, the HPML Non-Compliant determination is supported and additional regulatory violations (appraisal right-to-receive notice, appraisal delivery timing) are documented. The HVCRE determination is clean and the FZD determination is substantively compliant; remediation for those regimes is documentation-only and does not reflect substantive regulatory exposure.
